The finite family multiplier is an actual positive product of rational denominators. Each denominator divides that product, and the numerator identity gives an integer multiple. For a finite family of rational polynomials the same positive multiplier clears all supported coefficients. The constant coefficients must already be integral; every positive-degree term evaluated at D*z contains the needed multiplier and all remaining factors are integers. Every integer parameter, including negative ones, is covered. No integrality of a rational constant is silently assumed.

The rational exponential curve is the actual unitriangular exponential of the strict polynomial-scale matrix. Coefficient-ring compatibility proves evaluation at r is the original exponential of r*A. Its zero coefficient is the actual identity matrix. Uniform polynomial-family dilation over all direction/row/column indices proves every entry integral. The exact rational-integer-real membership equivalence then places these genuine exponential group elements in the original integer unitriangular lattice. Real scalar compatibility is proved, not assumed.

The rational structure is defined as the rational linear span of the actual logarithm image of the original integer group lattice. Its containment in the rational matrix-cast range follows from the retained proved rational lattice logarithms and an actual rational-linear matrix cast map. Strict support is proved on the whole span. The reverse inclusion for every rational strict matrix uses the newly proved actual integral exponential after a nonzero positive integer dilation, then divides only inside the rational linear span. This proves the structure equals exactly the real images of rational strict matrices; it does not prove that the unspanned integer logarithm set is additive.

Rationality of V is the usual real spanning condition for its intersection with this actual specified-lattice rational structure. Every rational generator has a strict rational preimage. Positive dilation produces an original lattice element whose logarithm is the corresponding nonzero real multiple inside V, so division inside the real span proves intersection logarithms span V. The converse follows from actual intersection membership in the ambient logarithm set. Finite-dimensional finite generation extracts a finite subset of actual intersection logarithms, without claiming independence or an adapted Malcev basis. The actual comap intersection is proved discrete and closed.

Exponential difference support congruence is proved both ways by successive support improvement of the genuine finite exponential. The actual product exp(A)*exp(B) differs from exp(A+B) only in depth k+1 when B has depth k. The inverse direction of the congruence recovers the actual product logarithm estimate. Consequently right multiplication by exp(B) is exact addition on its first support layer and leaves earlier support entries fixed, with no supplied BCH asymptotic equation.

The finite-integer-period compact-range theorem constructs a genuine finite real linear-combination parameter map, proves its continuity and surjectivity from the spanning family, and proves its standard integer parameter lattice maps into the actual period submodule. A compact standard parameter fundamental domain gives compact range in the unchanged target topology. The derived finite-dimensional version extracts finitely many actual period vectors from the proved full real span. Neither target metric nor target compactness is a premise.

In the abelian strict-matrix case only, vanishing of the actual associative Lie bracket proves commuting matrix inputs. The retained actual commuting exponential identity proves addition closure of the original lattice logarithms; the actual inverse exponential proves negation closure. The resulting integer submodule is constructed rather than postulated, and discreteness follows through the actual exponential homeomorphism into the original discrete group lattice. Its full real span follows by identifying its matrix image with the actual subgroup-lattice intersection logarithm set. No norm instance or additive lattice identification on an arbitrary nonabelian logarithm set is required.

Quotient equality uses actual lattice membership and multiplication cancellation, with no normality premise for the ambient lattice. The compact-period range theorem and actual surjectivity prove compactness of the natural restricted group quotient. The retained natural quotient inclusion theorem then proves a closed embedding and compact orbit in the original ambient lattice quotient.
